plainEnglishSummary: A gentle and common medicine used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain.

calmWarnings.title: Liver Health
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Taking more than the recommended dose can be hard on your liver. Always check other cold medicines, as they often contain hidden paracetamol.

plainEnglishSummary: Reduces pain, fever, and swelling by blocking the chemicals in your body that cause inflammation.

calmWarnings.title: Take with food
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Ibuprofen can irritate your stomach lining. Taking it with a meal or a glass of milk protects your stomach.

calmWarnings.title: Kidney Issues or High Blood Pressure
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: NSAIDs like Ibuprofen can raise blood pressure and make your kidneys work harder. Please check with your doctor first.

plainEnglishSummary: Relieves pain and reduces fever. Low doses are often used to protect the heart and prevent blood clots.

calmWarnings.title: Children and Teenagers
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: In children recovering from viral infections, aspirin can cause Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition affecting the liver and brain.

calmWarnings.title: Bleeding Risk
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Aspirin thins the blood. Avoid if you have stomach ulcers or are taking other blood thinners.

plainEnglishSummary: A long-lasting pain reliever that reduces swelling and stiffness, often used for joint and muscle pain.

calmWarnings.title: Heart and Stomach
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Long-term use can increase the risk of stomach ulcers and heart issues. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.

plainEnglishSummary: A strong anti-inflammatory medicine used for joint pain, arthritis, and muscle injuries.

calmWarnings.title: Heart Disease History
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Diclofenac can slightly increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with long-term use.

plainEnglishSummary: A targeted pain reliever that reduces inflammation with a lower risk of stomach ulcers than older pain medicines.

calmWarnings.title: Sulfa Allergy
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This medicine contains a sulfa component. Do not take it if you have a known allergy to sulfa drugs.

plainEnglishSummary: A once-daily medicine that reduces joint pain and swelling, commonly used for arthritis.

calmWarnings.title: Stomach Protection
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Like other NSAIDs, it can cause stomach bleeding. Take with food and report any black, tarry stools to your doctor.

plainEnglishSummary: A very strong, short-term pain reliever, often used after surgery or for severe kidney stones.

calmWarnings.title: Short-Term Use Only
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Never use for more than 5 days. Prolonged use severely increases the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney failure.

plainEnglishSummary: A powerful anti-inflammatory medicine used for severe joint pain and gout attacks.

calmWarnings.title: Brain Fog and Dizziness
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This medicine can cause headaches and confusion, especially in older adults. Avoid driving until you know how it affects you.

plainEnglishSummary: A long-acting anti-inflammatory medicine for chronic joint pain and stiffness.

calmWarnings.title: Sun Sensitivity
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Wear protective clothing and sunscreen when outdoors.

plainEnglishSummary: A prescription pain reliever for moderate to moderately severe pain, acting on the brain's pain signals.

calmWarnings.title: Risk of Dependence
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This is an opioid-like medicine. It can be habit-forming. Never share it, and take it exactly as prescribed.

calmWarnings.title: Serotonin Syndrome
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Do not mix with antidepressants, as it can cause a rare but dangerous condition called serotonin syndrome.

plainEnglishSummary: A mild opioid pain reliever, often combined with paracetamol for stronger pain relief.

calmWarnings.title: Breathing Issues
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Codeine can slow down your breathing. It is not safe for children under 12 or people with severe asthma.

plainEnglishSummary: Originally a seizure medicine, now widely used to calm nerve pain, like the burning or tingling from diabetes or shingles.

calmWarnings.title: Do Not Stop Suddenly
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Stopping this medicine abruptly can cause withdrawal symptoms or seizures. Always taper off with your doctor's guidance.

plainEnglishSummary: Calms overactive nerves to relieve nerve pain, fibromyalgia, and certain types of seizures.

calmWarnings.title: Dizziness and Weight Gain
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can cause significant dizziness and make you feel hungry. Stand up slowly to avoid falls.

plainEnglishSummary: A targeted medicine that narrows blood vessels in the brain to stop a migraine attack in its tracks.

calmWarnings.title: Heart Disease
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Because it narrows blood vessels, it is not safe for people with a history of heart attacks, angina, or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

plainEnglishSummary: A fast-acting migraine medicine that comes in a dissolving tablet for quick relief when you feel a migraine starting.

calmWarnings.title: Medication Overuse Headache
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Using this more than 10 days a month can actually cause more frequent headaches. Use only as directed.

plainEnglishSummary: A common, safe penicillin-type antibiotic that kills bacteria causing ear, throat, and urinary infections.

calmWarnings.title: Penicillin Allergy
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If you are allergic to penicillin, do not take this. It can cause a severe allergic reaction.

calmWarnings.title: Finish the Course
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Even if you feel better, finish all the pills. Stopping early can allow the bacteria to return stronger (antibiotic resistance).

plainEnglishSummary: A convenient antibiotic often taken for just 3 to 5 days to treat respiratory and skin infections.

calmWarnings.title: Heart Rhythm
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: In rare cases, it can affect the heart's electrical rhythm. Tell your doctor if you have a history of heart problems.

plainEnglishSummary: An antibiotic that fights specific bacteria and parasites, often used for stomach, dental, or vaginal infections.

calmWarnings.title: Zero Alcohol
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Do not drink any alcohol while taking this and for 3 days after. Mixing them causes severe vomiting, flushing, and rapid heartbeat.

plainEnglishSummary: A strong antibiotic used for serious bacterial infections, especially in the urinary tract or abdomen.

calmWarnings.title: Tendon Damage
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This class of antibiotics can rarely cause tendon inflammation or rupture, especially in people over 60 or those on steroids.

calmWarnings.title: Sun Sensitivity
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It makes your skin burn easily. Avoid direct sunlight and tanning beds.

plainEnglishSummary: A versatile antibiotic used for chest infections, acne, malaria prevention, and tick-borne diseases.

calmWarnings.title: Take Upright with Water
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can severely irritate your esophagus (food pipe). Take it with a full glass of water and do not lie down for 30 minutes.

calmWarnings.title: Pregnancy and Children
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can permanently stain developing teeth and affect bone growth in children under 8 and unborn babies.

plainEnglishSummary: A safe, first-generation antibiotic commonly used for skin, bone, and respiratory infections.

calmWarnings.title: Penicillin Cross-Reactivity
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If you have a severe penicillin allergy, there is a small chance you might also react to this medicine.

plainEnglishSummary: An antibiotic used for serious skin, dental, and bone infections, especially when patients are allergic to penicillin.

calmWarnings.title: Severe Diarrhea Warning
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If you develop watery or bloody diarrhea, stop taking it and call your doctor immediately, as it can indicate a serious colon infection.

plainEnglishSummary: A broad-spectrum antibiotic for pneumonia, sinus infections, and complicated urinary tract infections.

calmWarnings.title: Nerve and Tendon Risk
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Like ciprofloxacin, it carries a warning for tendon rupture and nerve damage. Report any joint pain or tingling immediately.

plainEnglishSummary: An antibiotic that concentrates in the urine, making it highly effective and specific for bladder infections.

calmWarnings.title: Take with Food
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Taking it with food or milk helps your body absorb it better and reduces stomach upset.

calmWarnings.title: Kidney Disease
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It does not work well and can be unsafe if your kidneys are not functioning properly.

plainEnglishSummary: A combination antibiotic often used for urinary tract infections and certain types of pneumonia.

calmWarnings.title: Sulfa Allergy
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Do not take if you are allergic to sulfa drugs. It can cause a severe skin rash.

calmWarnings.title: Stay Hydrated
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Drink plenty of water to prevent crystals from forming in your kidneys.

plainEnglishSummary: A powerful combination antibiotic. The clavulanate protects the amoxicillin from being destroyed by resistant bacteria.

calmWarnings.title: Stomach Upset
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This combination is more likely to cause diarrhea than amoxicillin alone. Taking it at the start of a meal helps.

plainEnglishSummary: An older, safe antibiotic often used for respiratory infections and acne, especially in pregnant women allergic to penicillin.

calmWarnings.title: Medicine Interactions
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It interacts with many other medicines (like statins). Always give your pharmacist a full list of what you take.

plainEnglishSummary: A well-tolerated antibiotic often prescribed for children and adults with ear, sinus, and throat infections.

calmWarnings.title: Harmless Red Stool
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If taken with iron supplements or iron-fortified formula, it can cause a harmless reddish color in the stool.

plainEnglishSummary: An antibiotic used for respiratory infections and as part of a combination therapy to cure stomach ulcers.

calmWarnings.title: Heart Rhythm Issues
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can affect the heart's electrical system. Avoid if you have a history of irregular heartbeat or are taking certain cholesterol medicines.

plainEnglishSummary: A 'proton pump inhibitor' that reduces the amount of acid your stomach makes, helping heal acid reflux and ulcers.

calmWarnings.title: Long-Term Use
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Using it daily for over a year can slightly increase the risk of bone fractures and lower vitamin B12 levels. Use the lowest dose that works.

plainEnglishSummary: Similar to omeprazole, it safely reduces stomach acid to heal the esophagus and prevent ulcers.

calmWarnings.title: Bone Health
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Long-term, high-dose use may be linked to a higher risk of hip, wrist, or spine fractures. Discuss calcium/vitamin D with your doctor.

plainEnglishSummary: An older acid reducer. *Note: Many brands were recalled due to impurities. Famotidine is now the preferred alternative.*

calmWarnings.title: Recall Notice
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Most ranitidine products were removed from the market due to a potential carcinogen (NDMA). Please ask your doctor about Famotidine instead.

plainEnglishSummary: A safe and effective acid reducer that works quickly to relieve heartburn and prevent stomach ulcers.

calmWarnings.title: Kidney Adjustment
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose, as the medicine is cleared by the kidneys.

plainEnglishSummary: A strong acid reducer often used when other heartburn medicines haven't worked well enough.

calmWarnings.title: Clopidogrel Interaction
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can make the blood thinner Clopidogrel (Plavix) less effective. Ask your doctor if you take both.

plainEnglishSummary: A fast-acting antacid that neutralizes stomach acid immediately to relieve heartburn. Also provides calcium.

calmWarnings.title: Kidney Stones
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Taking very high amounts regularly can increase the risk of kidney stones. Drink plenty of water.

plainEnglishSummary: A safe, gentle medicine that breaks up gas bubbles in your gut, making them easier to pass. It is not absorbed into the body.

calmWarnings.title: Symptom Check
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If your gas pain is severe or lasts more than a week, see a doctor, as it could be a sign of a different stomach issue.

plainEnglishSummary: Slows down the movement of the gut to quickly stop acute diarrhea.

calmWarnings.title: Bloody Diarrhea or Fever
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Do not use if you have a high fever or bloody stools, as this may indicate a bacterial infection that needs to be flushed out, not stopped.

plainEnglishSummary: Coats the stomach lining to relieve nausea, heartburn, indigestion, and diarrhea.

calmWarnings.title: Children with Viral Illness
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Contains salicylate (related to aspirin). Do not give to children or teenagers recovering from chickenpox or flu-like symptoms.

calmWarnings.title: Harmless Black Stool
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It will temporarily turn your stool or tongue black. This is normal and harmless.

plainEnglishSummary: A powerful anti-nausea medicine that blocks the chemicals in the body that trigger vomiting.

calmWarnings.title: Heart Rhythm
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: In rare cases, it can affect the heart's electrical rhythm. Tell your doctor if you have a history of heart problems.

plainEnglishSummary: Speeds up stomach emptying and blocks nausea signals, often used for severe acid reflux or gastroparesis.

calmWarnings.title: Movement Disorders
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Long-term use can cause uncontrollable muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia). Do not use for more than 12 weeks.

plainEnglishSummary: A gentle, non-habit-forming laxative that holds water in the stool to make it softer and easier to pass.

calmWarnings.title: Give it Time
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It is not a quick fix. It usually takes 1 to 3 days to work. Do not use for more than 7 days without a doctor's advice.

plainEnglishSummary: A daily, non-drowsy (for most) antihistamine that blocks the histamine causing your allergy symptoms.

calmWarnings.title: Mild Drowsiness
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: While labeled 'non-drowsy', about 10% of people do feel sleepy. Test how it affects you before driving.

plainEnglishSummary: A truly non-drowsy antihistamine that provides 24-hour relief from sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes.

calmWarnings.title: Liver Health
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: If you have liver or kidney disease, you may need to take this every other day instead of daily.

plainEnglishSummary: A fast-acting, older antihistamine that is very effective for severe allergies, itching, and as a short-term sleep aid.

calmWarnings.title: Older Adults
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can cause confusion, dizziness, and increase the risk of falls in people over 65. Safer alternatives exist.

calmWarnings.title: Drowsiness
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It causes significant drowsiness. Do not drive or operate machinery after taking it.

plainEnglishSummary: One of the least sedating antihistamines available, excellent for daytime allergy relief without brain fog.

calmWarnings.title: Fruit Juice Interaction
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Apple, orange, and grapefruit juice can block your body from absorbing this medicine. Take it with water only.

plainEnglishSummary: A powerful decongestant that shrinks swollen blood vessels in your nasal passages, helping you breathe freely.

calmWarnings.title: High Blood Pressure
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can raise blood pressure and heart rate. Avoid if you have hypertension, heart disease, or an overactive thyroid.

plainEnglishSummary: A cough suppressant that acts on the brain to reduce the urge to cough, helpful for dry, hacking coughs.
commonUses: Cough due to cold or flu

calmWarnings.title: MAOI Antidepressants
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Do not take if you are taking MAOI antidepressants, as it can cause a dangerous spike in body temperature and blood pressure.

plainEnglishSummary: An expectorant that thins and loosens mucus in your chest, making it easier to cough up and clear your airways.

calmWarnings.title: Drink Water
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This medicine works by drawing water into your mucus. Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day for it to work effectively.

plainEnglishSummary: A steroid nasal spray that reduces inflammation inside the nose, treating the root cause of allergy symptoms.

calmWarnings.title: Use Consistently
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It is not a quick fix. It may take several days of daily use to feel the full benefit. Aim the spray away from the center of your nose to avoid bleeding.

plainEnglishSummary: A daily tablet that blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that cause narrowing and swelling in the airways during asthma or allergies.

calmWarnings.title: Mood Changes
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Rarely, it can cause mood changes, agitation, or vivid dreams. Stop taking it and contact your doctor if you notice any mental health changes.

plainEnglishSummary: The first-line, safest, and most common medicine for Type 2 diabetes. It helps your body use insulin better and lowers sugar production in the liver.

calmWarnings.title: Take with Meals
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Taking it with food significantly reduces the chance of stomach upset and diarrhea.

calmWarnings.title: Vitamin B12
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Long-term use can lower Vitamin B12 levels. Your doctor may check this periodically.

plainEnglishSummary: A medicine that stimulates your pancreas to release more insulin, helping lower blood sugar levels.

calmWarnings.title: Low Blood Sugar (Hypoglycemia)
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can cause your blood sugar to drop too low, especially if you skip meals. Always carry a fast-acting sugar (like juice or candy) with you.

plainEnglishSummary: A long-acting 'basal' insulin that provides a steady, low level of insulin over 24 hours to keep fasting blood sugar stable.

calmWarnings.title: Never Share Pens
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Even with a new needle, never share an insulin pen with another person due to the risk of transmitting blood-borne diseases.

plainEnglishSummary: A 'calcium channel blocker' that relaxes and widens blood vessels, making it easier for the heart to pump and lowering blood pressure.

calmWarnings.title: Swollen Ankles
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It commonly causes fluid retention in the lower legs. If swelling is severe or sudden, contact your doctor.

plainEnglishSummary: An 'ACE inhibitor' that relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and protect the kidneys, especially in diabetics.

calmWarnings.title: Pregnancy
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It can cause severe harm or death to an unborn baby. Stop taking it and call your doctor immediately if you become pregnant.

calmWarnings.title: Dry Cough
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: A persistent, dry, tickly cough is a common side effect. If it bothers you, your doctor can switch you to a different class of medicine.

plainEnglishSummary: An 'ARB' that lowers blood pressure and protects the kidneys, often used if a patient cannot tolerate the cough from ACE inhibitors.

calmWarnings.title: Pregnancy
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Like Lisinopril, it is unsafe during pregnancy and can harm the developing baby.

plainEnglishSummary: A 'beta-blocker' that slows the heart rate and reduces the heart's workload, lowering blood pressure and preventing chest pain.

calmWarnings.title: Do Not Stop Suddenly
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Stopping abruptly can cause a dangerous rebound spike in heart rate and blood pressure, or even a heart attack. Always taper off with a doctor.

plainEnglishSummary: A 'statin' that lowers 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) and reduces the risk of heart attack and stroke by stabilizing plaque in arteries.

calmWarnings.title: Muscle Pain
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Rarely, it can cause muscle inflammation. If you develop unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, contact your doctor immediately.

calmWarnings.title: Grapefruit
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Eating large amounts of grapefruit can increase the level of this medicine in your blood, raising the risk of side effects.

plainEnglishSummary: A potent statin that effectively lowers bad cholesterol and raises good cholesterol, offering strong heart protection.

calmWarnings.title: Muscle and Liver Monitoring
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Your doctor will likely order a simple blood test periodically to check your liver and muscle health while on this medicine.

plainEnglishSummary: A synthetic version of the natural thyroid hormone. It replaces what your body isn't making enough of, restoring normal energy and metabolism.

calmWarnings.title: Take on Empty Stomach
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: For best absorption, take it first thing in the morning with water, and wait at least 30-60 minutes before eating or taking other medicines.

commonSideEffects: Heat sensitivity (if dose is too high)

plainEnglishSummary: A daily medicine that lowers uric acid levels in the blood, preventing painful gout attacks and kidney stones.

calmWarnings.title: Do Not Start During an Attack
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Starting this medicine during an active gout flare can make the pain worse. Wait until the flare has completely settled.

plainEnglishSummary: A powerful blood thinner that prevents dangerous blood clots from forming in the heart, lungs, or legs.

calmWarnings.title: Bleeding Risk & Diet
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It makes you bleed more easily. Avoid contact sports. Keep your intake of Vitamin K (leafy greens) consistent, as sudden changes affect how the medicine works.

plainEnglishSummary: An SSRI antidepressant that increases serotonin in the brain, helping to improve mood, sleep, and appetite over time.

calmWarnings.title: Takes Time to Work
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It usually takes 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it just because you don't feel better in the first week.

calmWarnings.title: Do Not Stop Abruptly
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Stopping suddenly can cause 'discontinuation syndrome' (dizziness, brain zaps). Always taper with your doctor.

plainEnglishSummary: A highly targeted SSRI antidepressant, often preferred for its effectiveness in treating generalized anxiety and depression with fewer side effects.

calmWarnings.title: Initial Anxiety
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Some people feel slightly more anxious during the first 1-2 weeks. This is normal and usually fades as your body adjusts.

plainEnglishSummary: A well-known SSRI antidepressant that is slightly more 'activating', making it a good choice for people with depression who also feel very fatigued.

calmWarnings.title: Insomnia
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Because it can be energizing, it is usually best taken in the morning to avoid trouble sleeping at night.

plainEnglishSummary: An SNRI antidepressant that works on both serotonin and norepinephrine, often used when SSRIs haven't been fully effective.

calmWarnings.title: Blood Pressure Monitoring
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: At higher doses, it can raise blood pressure. Your doctor should check your BP regularly.

plainEnglishSummary: A unique antidepressant that works on dopamine and norepinephrine. It does not cause weight gain or sexual side effects, and is also used to help quit smoking.

calmWarnings.title: Seizure Risk
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It lowers the seizure threshold. Do not take it if you have a history of seizures, eating disorders (bulimia/anorexia), or are abruptly stopping alcohol.

plainEnglishSummary: An antidepressant that is uniquely helpful for people who struggle with both depression and severe insomnia or poor appetite.

calmWarnings.title: Weight Gain and Drowsiness
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It strongly increases appetite and causes sleepiness. It is usually taken right before bed to turn this side effect into a benefit.

plainEnglishSummary: A fast-acting benzodiazepine that calms the central nervous system, providing rapid relief from severe panic and anxiety.

calmWarnings.title: High Risk of Dependence
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: This medicine is habit-forming and should only be used short-term. Never mix it with alcohol or opioid pain medicines, as the combination can be fatal.

plainEnglishSummary: A benzodiazepine used for short-term relief of severe anxiety symptoms or to help with sleep before medical procedures.

calmWarnings.title: Older Adults
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It significantly increases the risk of confusion, falls, and fractures in older adults. Safer alternatives are strongly recommended.

plainEnglishSummary: A 'Z-drug' sleep aid that helps you fall asleep faster by slowing down brain activity.

calmWarnings.title: Complex Sleep Behaviors
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Rarely, people may sleepwalk, sleep-eat, or sleep-drive without remembering it. If this happens, stop the medicine and call your doctor immediately.

calmWarnings.title: Take Right Before Bed
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Only take it if you can dedicate a full 7-8 hours to sleep. Do not take it in the middle of the night.

plainEnglishSummary: A natural hormone supplement that signals to your brain that it is time to sleep, helpful for jet lag or shifting sleep schedules.

calmWarnings.title: Less is More
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Lower doses (0.5mg to 3mg) are often more effective than high doses (10mg), which can cause grogginess and vivid dreams.

plainEnglishSummary: An antihistamine with strong calming properties, often prescribed as a safe, non-habit-forming alternative for anxiety or itching.

calmWarnings.title: Drowsiness
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: It causes significant drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you.

plainEnglishSummary: An atypical antipsychotic that, at very low doses, is sometimes used off-label for severe, treatment-resistant insomnia or anxiety.

calmWarnings.title: Metabolic Changes
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Even at low doses, it can cause weight gain, increased blood sugar, and cholesterol changes over time. Regular monitoring is required.

plainEnglishSummary: A non-habit-forming anti-anxiety medicine that takes a few weeks to build up in your system, making it a safe long-term option.

calmWarnings.title: Takes Time to Work
calmWarnings.plainEnglishWhy: Unlike Xanax, it does not work instantly. It may take 2 to 4 weeks of daily use to feel the full calming effect.
